blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Plan three bounded release-convergence implementation tasks: restore the preserved authored cemetery's spatial/compositional integrity, bound dense-wave runtime cost, and complete the ordinary seven-to-ten-minute run with visual upgrade choices, authoritative transaction state, Result, and clean Retry.

diagnosis.root_cause: Prior camera-only reframing did not resolve the underlying authored-world composition: the preserved cemetery instance remains mausoleum-dominant, sparse, and weakly layered, with insufficient human-scale and warm/cool hierarchy. Dense-wave cost bounds and complete-run/upgrade transaction behavior also remain unclosed release obligations.

stop_conditions: Do not replace, split, hide, extract, or surgically modify the preserved authored cemetery package.
Do not schedule deferred backlog gaps or unrelated product families.
Stop after the three candidate implementation tasks have explicit acceptance and evidence matrices; GameLoop Runtime and Tester retain recapture, verdict, and issue-closure authority.
Preserve passing native_godot_project and host_godot_boot baselines.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different strategy from prior transform tuning: repair authored-map instance binding, native landmark presentation, outer datum, and spatial contracts first; isolate dense-wave lifecycle costs; then make run-state and upgrade-choice transactions explicit and retestable.

code: Run focused Godot/static checks for authored scene bindings, native collision/navigation/spawn anchors, run-state reset, draft single-commit/overflow handling, dense-wave caps, and deterministic cleanup.
Verify the preserved authored-map hierarchy and assets are unchanged; reject proxy roads/floors, destructive asset surgery, visible placeholders, and candidate debug UI in shipped scenes.
Inspect candidate runtime logs for repeated errors, duplicate timers, stale pause reasons, or post-terminal spawning.
runtime: Host/Tester recapture boot/integrity, spawn, critical route, cardinal landmark, perimeter, ordinary movement/movement replay, dense final wave at 1920x1080, level-up draft/selection/resume, five-wave/Bellkeeper completion, Result, failure, Retry, and Return to Title.

Collect runtime_state digests, scene/spatial bounds, collision/visibility/navigation probes, frame-time and active-count counters, input-focus receipts, upgrade mutation/build snapshots, and runtime logs; recapture failed cells with identical framing and a changed state/time/input step.
Require three distinct successful ordinary complete routes for viable build-shape qualification; do not substitute diagnostic preparation, synthetic rows, or failure routes.
visual: Compare shipped gameplay views against the bound Mournlight reference: dense layered cemetery, readable Warden and keeper post/mausoleum/cracked bell, human scale, warm lantern versus cool moonlight, clear escape lanes, external depth, and no void or stand-ins.

Inspect upgrade cards and full-screen Result/Retry pages at native, fullscreen/windowed, and supported UI scales for authored iconography, truthful current-to-new deltas (no more than three), restrained hierarchy, and complete keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states.
Inspect adjacent combat, dense-wave, boss, Result, and Retry frames for readable telegraphs, bounded effects, stable landmark visibility, and clean reset composition.

done_when: The intact authored cemetery remains the sole authoritative visual environment and the playable footprint is expanded to a larger traversable scale.
A coherent external world and external depth are visible beyond the playable perimeter without void, proxy-floor, or empty finished-art planes dominating gameplay.
The central building and other landmark anchors (keeper post, mausoleum, cracked bell) remain readable from spawn, critical route, and cardinal views.
Visible geometry and collision agree: ordinary movement and movement replay cannot pass through landmarks, encounter invisible barriers, or leave the authored boundary/perimeter.
No landmark disappearance or camera occlusion drift occurs during ordinary movement; escape lanes, human-scale silhouettes, and warm lantern versus cool moonlight hierarchy read at shipped framing.
Tester can black-box traverse spawn→route→landmark→perimeter and white-box verify stable collision, visibility, navigation, and boundary predicates.
tasks.instructions: Repair the authored cemetery through direct scene-instance/binding and spatial-contract work rather than another camera-transform-only pass. Keep native streets, structures, props, materials, and landmarks intact; rebase spawn, objective anchors, navigation, collision, and one outer gameplay datum on native streets. Expand to a larger traversable scale, establish external world/external depth, and rebalance the central building/landmark, human-scale framing, escape lanes, and warm/cool lighting hierarchy using the existing authored package and candidate-owned presentation bindings. Verify collision, disappearance, occlusion, boundary/perimeter, ordinary movement, and movement replay at spawn, route, cardinal, and edge views. Do not add proxy roads/floors or perform destructive asset surgery.
tasks.title: Restore authored cemetery scale, landmark visibility, and spatial integrity

done_when: At 1920x1080, a representative final-wave replay with 25–40 ordinary enemies plus all weapon families, pickups, animation, VFX, lights, UI, and audio maintains a stable frame-time distribution within the existing performance budget.
Wave director and enemy motion enforce bounded live counts and spawn safety; projectile, pickup, VFX, health-bar, and drop lifecycles reclaim or reuse instances deterministically.
Three complete retry cycles show no active-node, timer, signal, allocation, or effect growth after death, wave transition, victory/failure, reset, and Retry.
Automatic combat cadence and readable telegraphs remain intact, and runtime logs contain no repeated errors or duplicate processing.
Tester can replay the same dense scenario and compare frame time, active-enemy/projectile/pickup/VFX counts, and cleanup receipts.
tasks.instructions: Profile and harden candidate-owned dense-wave systems without changing the survivor-like combat contract. Bound wave spawning, enemy-neighbor steering, projectile/drop/pickup/VFX and vitality-bar churn with caps, pooling or deterministic reuse, staggered work, and explicit cleanup on death, wave transition, terminal state, reset, and Retry. Preserve readable automatic targeting, attack cadence, telegraphs, and all three weapon identities. Add focused candidate-owned counters/guards or debug hooks so Tester can validate sustained 1920x1080 final-wave cost and three-retry growth, while keeping shipped behavior free of debug presentation.
tasks.title: Bound dense-wave spawn, motion, effects, and cleanup

done_when: A complete ordinary seven-to-ten-minute route runs through five escalating waves and the Bellkeeper final encounter to a Result state showing time, level, defeats, damage dealt/taken, selected upgrades, and victory or failure.
At least three distinct viable successful build shapes are produced by ordinary complete routes; failure routes prove failure/Result/Retry only and are not counted as viable builds.
Level-up opens exactly one paused three-choice draft per threshold, preserves overflow experience, excludes ineligible choices, and applies the selected upgrade exactly once before gameplay resumes.

Replace text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices with an authored visual hierarchy: each option leads with a recognizable weapon/upgrade silhouette or authored icon, then compact stat icons and truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas.
Current values never show NEW or LOCKED placeholders; unchanged, zero-placeholder, locked-to-equipped, unrelated, and exhaustive rows are omitted and copy remains restrained.
Keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, hover, unavailable, and selected states are complete, visually distinct, and readable without resizing cards.

The selected build persists into Result and Retry, and Retry/Return to Title reset actors, pools, timers, signals, pause ownership, audio, input focus, upgrades, XP, and result flags to a clean fresh run without application restart.
Tester can black-box verify the draft→select→resume→Result→Retry matrix and inspect authoritative build mutation/persistence.
tasks.instructions: Complete the ordinary release route and its build-choice surface as one authoritative transaction family. Wire run_controller, complete-run ledger, upgrade draft controller/UI, pause ownership, Result, Retry, and title transitions so a seven-to-ten-minute five-wave/Bellkeeper run records truthful statistics and build summary, and every restart returns to a clean baseline. Replace text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices with an authored visual hierarchy: silhouettes/icons first, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values for at most three decision-relevant deltas, restrained copy, and complete keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states. Filter eligibility, debounce held confirm, preserve overflow XP, commit once, resume only after mutation, and retain the chosen build through Result and Retry. Keep UI and effects as readers of authoritative state.
tasks.title: Complete run lifecycle and visual, truthful upgrade transactions
